questions.s: In environmental science this week, we are studying plastic pollution. Every year, millions of tons of plastic packaging end up in landfills and oceans, where they can remain for centuries. Communities have tried two broad approaches. Some ban certain single-use items, such as plastic bags and straws. Others keep these items legal but offer incentives, for example a small refund when people return bottles for recycling. Which approach do you think is more effective at reducing plastic waste, and why?
questions.e: I agree with Olga that incentives are the better approach, although I would add a different reason. Bans only work for a small number of items that have easy substitutes, such as bags and straws. Most plastic waste, however, comes from packaging for food, cleaning products and electronics, which cannot simply be banned without causing serious problems for shops and customers. A refund system can be applied to a much wider range of products. Another advantage is that incentives create jobs and businesses. When large amounts of clean, sorted plastic are returned, recycling companies have a steady supply of material and can afford to invest in better technology. Hamza is right that a few cents may not motivate everyone, but the refund can be set high enough to make returning items worthwhile. In short, incentives can reach more types of plastic than bans ever could.

ps.name: Hamza
ps.text: Bans are more effective because they remove the problem completely. If shops are not allowed to give out plastic bags, people quickly get used to bringing their own. Incentives depend on people remembering to do the right thing, and many of them simply won't bother, especially when the refund is only a few cents.

ps.name: Olga
ps.text: I prefer incentives. Bans can create new problems, since some replacement products, like thick paper bags, also need a lot of energy to produce. A refund system keeps useful plastic items available but makes sure they are collected and recycled. In my home country, almost every bottle is returned because people see the money as their own.

questions.s: In urban planning, one of the most debated questions is how to use limited street space. Many cities are now turning car lanes into protected bicycle lanes. Supporters say this makes streets safer and cleaner, while opponents point to heavier traffic and difficulties for businesses that rely on deliveries. Imagine your city is considering replacing one car lane on its main shopping street with a bike lane. Would you support this change? Explain why or why not.
questions.e: I understand Chen's worry about local shops, but I would support the bike lane. In fact, I think it could help businesses rather than hurt them. People on bicycles travel slowly enough to notice shop windows, and it is very easy for them to stop, lock their bike and go inside. Drivers, on the other hand, often pass by because they cannot find parking. As a result, cyclists and pedestrians may visit local shops more often, even if they spend a little less on each visit. The street would also become quieter and more pleasant, which encourages people to stay longer, sit in cafes and meet friends. To deal with deliveries, the city could allow trucks to load and unload in special zones early in the morning before the street gets busy. With careful planning, the main shopping street could become a place people enjoy visiting, not just driving through.

ps.name: Yuki
ps.text: I would support it. Many people would like to cycle, but they are afraid of riding next to fast cars. A protected lane makes them feel safe, and once they start cycling, there are fewer cars on the road. In the end, traffic can actually improve because each cyclist is one less car looking for a parking space.

ps.name: Chen
ps.text: I would not support it on a shopping street. Shops need trucks to deliver goods every morning, and many customers drive in from other areas because they buy heavy items. If there is less space for cars, these customers may go to a large mall outside the city instead, and small local shops could lose a lot of business.

questions.s: In our course on technology and society, we have been discussing how mobile phones affect young people's lives. Some schools now require students to lock their phones away from the start of the school day until it ends. Others allow phones during breaks or let teachers decide whether phones can be used for classwork. Do you think schools should ban students' phones for the whole school day, or should they allow phones at certain times? Explain your view.
questions.e: Daniel makes a fair point about parents, but I support a full-day ban for most schools. The main reason, in my opinion, is that a clear rule is much easier to follow than a partial one. When phones are allowed at certain times, teachers must constantly check whether students are using them at the right moment, and arguments start over small things, such as sending one message just before the bell. A complete ban removes this daily conflict and lets teachers focus on teaching. Moreover, a ban reduces pressure on students who do not own expensive phones, because nobody can show off a new model at school. As for contacting children, parents can still call the school office in an emergency, just as families did before smartphones existed. If teachers need technology for a lesson, the school can provide tablets that are used only for learning.

ps.name: Aisha
ps.text: A full-day ban is the best option. Even during breaks, students who have phones tend to stare at their screens instead of talking or playing together. Without phones, break time becomes a chance to make friends and get some exercise, and students come back to class feeling more relaxed and ready to learn.

ps.name: Daniel
ps.text: I think phones should be allowed at some times. They can be useful learning tools, for example for looking up a word, taking a photo of the board or using a science app. Also, many parents want to be able to contact their children during the day, especially if plans change and someone else has to pick them up.

questions.s: Our psychology unit this week is about motivation and goal setting. Some experts advise people to set ambitious long-term goals, such as running a marathon or becoming fluent in a language within a year, because a big target gives life direction. Others argue that it is better to focus on small daily habits, like jogging for ten minutes or learning five new words, without worrying about the final result. Which approach do you think leads to greater success, and why?
questions.e: I agree with Ravi that small daily habits lead to greater success, but for a slightly different reason. In my view, the biggest advantage of habits is that they are easier to recover from when something goes wrong. Life is unpredictable: people get sick, travel or have a busy week at work. If someone's goal is to lose ten kilograms by summer and they miss two weeks, they may feel they have already failed and quit completely. With a habit, missing a day is a small problem, and they simply start again tomorrow. Habits also build a new identity. A person who walks every morning slowly begins to see themselves as an active person, and this belief makes healthy choices feel natural rather than forced. Elena is right that a goal provides direction, so perhaps the best plan is to choose a goal but measure success by whether the daily habit is completed.

ps.name: Elena
ps.text: I believe big goals are more powerful. When I decided to pass a difficult exam, that clear target made me organize my whole week around studying. Small habits are nice, but without a larger purpose, it is easy to stop doing them when you are tired, because you don't see why they matter.

ps.name: Ravi
ps.text: For me, small habits work better. Big goals can feel so far away that people give up when they don't see quick progress. When I started doing just ten push-ups a day, it felt easy, so I never skipped it. Months later, I was much stronger than I had ever been with my old, ambitious plans.

questions.s: In public health, we often look for ways to help people become more physically active, since regular exercise lowers the risk of many diseases. Two common strategies are workplace programs, such as free gym memberships or walking challenges for employees, and changes to city design, such as safer sidewalks, parks and bike paths. If a city had money for only one of these strategies, which do you think would do more to increase physical activity among adults? Please explain your reasoning.
questions.e: Like Tariq, I would spend the money on city design, and I have an additional reason. Changes to the environment last for decades, while workplace programs depend on a company's budget each year. A new park or bike path can keep encouraging people to move for thirty or forty years, long after a gym membership offer has been cancelled. In addition, better city design benefits children. When parents feel that the streets are safe, they let their children walk or cycle to school, and children who grow up being active are more likely to stay active as adults. In this way, one investment improves the health of two generations. Grace's example shows that workplace challenges can work, but they reach a smaller group and may disappear when a company changes its priorities. For a city choosing only one strategy, the long-lasting option seems wiser.

ps.name: Grace
ps.text: Workplace programs would have a bigger effect. Adults spend most of their week at work, so that is where we can reach them. When my mother's company started a step challenge with small prizes, almost everyone in her office joined, and many of them still walk at lunchtime even though the challenge ended long ago.

ps.name: Tariq
ps.text: I would choose city design. Workplace programs help only people with office jobs, but sidewalks and parks are available to everyone, including retired people and those who work at home. If walking to the shop is safe and pleasant, people exercise without even planning to, simply as part of their daily routine.

questions.s: In media studies this week, we are examining how news organizations pay for their work. For years, most news websites were free and earned money from advertising. Today, many of them place their articles behind a paywall, which means readers must buy a subscription to read more than a few stories each month. Some people believe paywalls are necessary for good journalism, while others think news should be free for everyone. What is your opinion? Should news websites charge readers for access?
questions.e: I agree with Nadia that news websites should be allowed to charge readers, although Omar's concern about fairness is important. One reason that has not been mentioned is independence. When a news organization depends on a few large advertisers, it may hesitate to publish stories that criticize those companies, because it fears losing their money. If thousands of ordinary readers pay a small amount each month, no single advertiser has that kind of power, and journalists can report more freely. At the same time, there are ways to keep paywalls fair. Many newspapers already offer cheap student subscriptions, and public libraries can provide free digital access to their members. Some websites also make urgent information, such as weather warnings or health advice, free for everyone. With these exceptions, paywalls can support high-quality journalism without leaving people with low incomes behind.

ps.name: Nadia
ps.text: Yes, they should charge. Investigating a serious story can take reporters months of work, and that is expensive. When news depends only on advertising, websites are tempted to publish shocking headlines just to get clicks. Subscriptions allow them to focus on careful, accurate reporting, because readers are paying for quality rather than for excitement.

ps.name: Omar
ps.text: I think news should remain free. Not everyone can afford several subscriptions, and students or people with low incomes would only have access to free sources, which are often less reliable. If important information is locked away, society becomes divided between people who are well informed and people who are not.

questions.s: In our economics course, we have been studying the costs and benefits of tourism. Popular destinations earn a lot of money from visitors, but large crowds can also raise housing prices, damage historic sites and put pressure on public services. To manage this, some cities charge a small tourist tax for every night a visitor stays in a hotel. Do you think popular cities should charge a tourist tax? Explain why or why not.
questions.e: In my opinion, popular cities should charge a tourist tax, and I would add a point that neither Isabel nor Jin mentioned: the tax can be used to spread visitors more evenly. A city could charge a higher fee during the busiest summer months and a lower fee, or none at all, in the quieter season. This would encourage some travelers to come at a different time, which reduces crowds at famous sites and gives local businesses customers all year instead of only for a few weeks. I understand Jin's worry that families might choose another destination, but I doubt a small nightly fee is enough to change most people's plans, since flights and hotels cost far more. As long as the city explains clearly how the money is spent, for example on parks or museum repairs, visitors are likely to accept the tax as fair.

questions.s: This week in our education course, we are looking at different forms of assessment. Many instructors now give group projects, in which three or four students research a topic together and receive one shared grade. Other instructors prefer individual assignments, such as essays and exams, because they show exactly what each student has learned. Which type of assignment do you think better prepares students for life after university: group projects or individual assignments? Explain why.
questions.e: I side with Fatima that group projects are better preparation for life after university, but I would like to add another benefit. Group projects teach students to work with people who think differently. In an individual essay, I only have to convince myself that my ideas are good. In a group, I have to listen to classmates from other countries or other majors who may approach the problem in a completely different way. For example, in a marketing project, an engineering student in my group suggested testing our idea with a simple survey, which made our final presentation much stronger. This kind of cooperation is exactly what happens in international companies. Marco is right that some students avoid their share of the work, but instructors can solve this by asking each member to write a short report on what they did and grading part of the project individually.

ps.name: Marco

questions.s: In our business course, we are studying customer loyalty, which is the tendency of customers to keep buying from the same company. Loyal customers are valuable because they spend more over time and recommend the company to friends. Some managers believe loyalty depends mainly on product quality, while others think excellent customer service matters more. In your opinion, which is more important for keeping customers loyal: the quality of the product or the quality of the service? Please explain.
questions.e: Although Leila is right that a bad product will drive customers away, I agree with Samuel that service is more important for loyalty. My reason is that service matters most at the moment when something goes wrong. Every company makes mistakes eventually: a delivery arrives late, or a product has a defect. What customers remember is how the company responds. If an airline loses my suitcase but the staff apologize, keep me informed and deliver it to my hotel the same evening, I may actually trust that airline more than before. On the other hand, if I spend an hour on the phone and nobody helps me, I will probably never fly with them again, no matter how comfortable their seats are. In other words, quality may bring customers in the first time, but service is what turns a problem into a reason to stay.

ps.name: Samuel
ps.text: I think service matters more. These days, many products are very similar in quality and price, so service is what makes one company stand out. questions.s: Our sociology class has been discussing how people learn the skills and values they need in life. In the past, young people learned mostly from older family members and neighbors. Today, many young people turn to friends of their own age, often through social media and online communities, for advice on everything from studying to careers. Do you think young people today learn more useful lessons from older generations or from their peers? Explain your opinion.
questions.e: Victor has a point about technology, but I agree with Hana that older generations offer the more useful lessons. In my view, the most valuable things older people teach are not technical skills but ways of dealing with people. My aunt, for instance, taught me how to calm down before answering an angry message and how to apologize properly when I am wrong. These lessons do not become out of date, because human relationships have not changed very much, even if the tools we use to communicate have. Peers, by contrast, often have the same blind spots as we do, since they are at the same stage of life and are dealing with similar worries. Their advice can feel comforting, but it rarely challenges us. Older people have seen how similar situations ended, so they can warn us about consequences that young people cannot yet imagine.

Experience like that cannot be replaced by advice from people who are just as young as I am.

questions.s: In environmental science, we have been studying how to protect endangered animal species. One approach is to breed animals in zoos and wildlife centers and later return some of them to the wild. Another approach is to protect the natural habitats where these animals live, for example by creating national parks and limiting logging or farming nearby. If a conservation organization could fund only one of these approaches, which do you think it should choose, and why?
questions.e: I agree with Ingrid that protecting habitats is the better choice, and I would add an economic reason. Breeding programs are very expensive for each animal, because the animals need special food, veterinary care and large enclosures for many years. The same amount of money could protect a large area of land, and protected areas can even earn money of their own. For example, many national parks attract visitors who pay entrance fees and hire local guides, which gives nearby communities a reason to keep the forest healthy instead of cutting it down. This makes habitat protection more sustainable over the long term. Kenji is correct that captive breeding can rescue a species in an emergency, but it should be a last resort. If we protect habitats early, fewer species will ever reach the point where they can survive only in a zoo.

ps.name: Ingrid
ps.text: The organization should protect habitats. Even if a zoo breeds hundreds of animals, they have nowhere to go if their forest or wetland has been destroyed. Protecting a habitat also saves many other species at the same time, including plants and insects that zoos never pay attention to.

ps.name: Kenji
ps.text: I would fund breeding programs. When a species has only a few dozen animals left, protecting land is too slow to save it. Zoos can keep a population safe from disease and hunting while scientists study it. Some animals that were almost extinct in the wild survived only because they were bred in captivity.

questions.s: Growing cities need more housing, and urban planners must decide where and how to build it. One option is to build upward, with tall apartment buildings in or near the city center. Another option is to build outward, creating new neighborhoods of houses with gardens on the edge of the city. Each choice affects transportation, the environment and people's quality of life. In your view, which option should a growing city choose, and why?
questions.e: I agree with Lina that a growing city should build upward, and I would like to add a reason related to public costs. Every new neighborhood on the edge of a city needs new roads, water pipes, electricity lines, schools and fire stations. These are extremely expensive to build and maintain, and the cost is shared by all taxpayers, including people who live in the center. Tall buildings, in contrast, can use infrastructure that already exists. A city that builds upward therefore spends less money on construction and has more to spend on parks, libraries and public transport. Diego's point about families is understandable, but tall buildings do not have to mean small, dark apartments. Planners can require larger family apartments, shared courtyards and playgrounds on the ground floor, so that children still have safe places to play close to home.

When many people live close together near the center, it also becomes practical to run frequent buses and trains, and people can walk to work, shops and schools instead of driving everywhere.

ps.name: Diego

questions.s: In technology and society, we have been exploring how artificial intelligence is changing education. Several apps now act as personal tutors: they explain problems step by step, answer questions at any hour and adjust exercises to each learner's level. Some people predict that these tools will greatly reduce the need for human tutors. Others believe that human tutors offer something technology cannot. For a high school student who needs extra help in math, would an AI tutor or a human tutor be more helpful? Why?
questions.e: I agree with Felix that a human tutor would be more helpful, but my reason is a little different. I think the biggest advantage of a human tutor is accountability. When a student knows that a real person is expecting them on Tuesday at five o'clock and will ask whether they finished their practice problems, they are much more likely to do the work. An app, on the other hand, is easy to ignore; the student can simply close it when the questions get difficult, and nobody will notice. Many teenagers know they should study, but they need someone to keep them on track. Zara is right that AI tutors are cheaper and always available, so I think they work best as an extra tool between sessions. For a student who is really struggling, however, regular meetings with a human tutor provide the structure and commitment that make improvement possible.

ps.name: Felix
ps.text: A human tutor is better. Many students who struggle with math are not just confused about the steps; they are nervous and have lost confidence. A good human tutor notices when a student is frustrated, encourages them and changes the lesson. An app cannot really understand how a teenager feels.

questions.s: In our psychology course, we are studying decision making. Some research suggests that groups make better decisions because members share knowledge and catch each other's mistakes. Other research shows that groups sometimes make worse choices, for example when people agree with the majority simply to avoid conflict. Think about important decisions, such as choosing a strategy for a project or planning a major purchase. Do you think people generally make better decisions alone or in a group? Explain your view.
questions.e: I believe groups generally make better decisions, as Beatriz suggests, but only if they are organized well. Arjun is right that loud members can dominate a meeting, yet this problem has a simple solution: each person can write down their own ideas before the discussion starts. This way, quiet members contribute, and nobody is influenced by the majority too early. Another benefit of groups that has not been mentioned is commitment. When people help make a decision, they understand the reasons behind it and feel responsible for its success. For instance, if a team chooses its own project schedule, members are more likely to meet the deadlines than if a manager simply announces the plan. A person deciding alone may choose quickly, but if others have to carry out the decision, they may not support it fully. For important decisions that affect several people, a well-run group is the wiser choice.

ps.name: Beatriz
ps.text: Groups make better decisions. Each person sees a problem from a different angle, so a group can think of more options and notice risks that one person might miss. When my family planned a long trip, my brother realized our passports needed renewing, something I had completely forgotten while I was busy comparing hotels.

ps.text: I think people decide better alone. In groups, the loudest person often controls the discussion, and quieter people keep their good ideas to themselves. questions.s: This week in public health, we are discussing young people's diets. Many teenagers drink several sugary drinks a day, which is linked to tooth decay and weight gain. Schools have tried different responses. Some have removed sugary drinks from their cafeterias and vending machines entirely. Others still sell them but display clear information about sugar content and offer cheaper healthy alternatives, such as water and milk. Which approach do you think is better for students' health, and why?
questions.e: I agree with Chloe that schools should remove sugary drinks completely, and I want to add a point about the message schools send. A school is supposed to teach healthy habits in its science and sports classes. If the same school then sells soda in the cafeteria, students receive mixed messages, and the lessons seem less serious. Removing the drinks shows that the school really believes what it teaches. Mohammed makes a fair argument about the shop across the street, but I do not think most students would leave campus every day just to buy a drink, especially younger ones who are not allowed to go out at lunchtime. Even if some do, the total amount of sugar they consume would still fall. Of course, schools should also teach students to read food labels, but this education works best when the school environment supports it instead of contradicting it.

ps.name: Chloe
ps.text: Removing sugary drinks is the better approach. Teenagers often choose what tastes good, not what is healthy, even when they know the facts. If the drinks are simply not available at school, students drink water instead, and over time they may lose the habit of having soda with every meal.

ps.name: Mohammed
ps.text: I prefer giving information and cheaper alternatives. If schools remove these drinks, students will just buy them at the shop across the street. Teaching them to read labels and make good choices is more useful, because after they leave school, nobody will be there to remove unhealthy products for them.

questions.s: In media studies, we have been looking at how online reviews influence what people buy. Before choosing a restaurant, hotel or product, many consumers now read ratings and comments written by strangers. Supporters say that reviews give ordinary people power and push companies to improve. Critics point out that some reviews are fake, paid for, or written by people who are simply in a bad mood. Overall, do you think online reviews help consumers make better choices, or do they mislead them more often than they help?
questions.e: Maya is right that extreme opinions appear more often, but I still believe online reviews help consumers more than they mislead them. One benefit that hasn't been mentioned is the way companies respond in public. Many businesses now reply to complaints online, and these replies tell me a lot. If a restaurant answers a negative review politely and explains how it fixed the problem, I feel more confident eating there. If it attacks the customer, I know to stay away. This conversation between customers and businesses did not exist before review websites. In addition, careful readers can avoid most of the problems Maya describes. Instead of looking only at the star rating, I read several reviews from the middle of the scale, which usually describe the normal experience in a calm way. When reviews are read thoughtfully, they are one of the most useful tools a modern consumer has.

pt: Clearly states that reviews help more than they mislead

Responds to Maya by name and explains a reading strategy that answers her concern
Uses a balanced, reasoned tone with concrete examples

ps.name: Sven
ps.text: Online reviews mostly help. When I booked a hotel last summer, several reviews mentioned that the rooms facing the street were very noisy, so I asked for a quiet room. That kind of detail never appears in an advertisement. With hundreds of reviews, a few fake ones don't change the overall picture.

ps.name: Maya
ps.text: I think reviews are often misleading. People usually write reviews only when they are extremely happy or extremely angry, so the ratings don't show the normal experience. I once avoided a cafe because of a few terrible reviews, but when a friend took me there, the food and service were excellent.

questions.s: In our economics course, we are studying how companies try to influence consumer behavior. Many supermarkets, airlines and coffee shops run loyalty programs, which give customers points, discounts or free items in exchange for repeat purchases. These programs are extremely common, but economists disagree about who really gains from them. Do you think loyalty programs mainly benefit consumers, or do they mainly benefit the companies that run them? Explain your opinion.
questions.e: I agree with Ethan that loyalty programs mainly benefit companies, and I would add one more reason: data. Every time customers scan a loyalty card, the company records what they bought, when and how often. This information is extremely valuable. It allows the company to decide which products to stock, how to set prices and which personal offers will tempt each customer to spend more. In a sense, customers are paying for their small discounts with detailed information about their own habits, and most of them never think about it. Rosa is right that families who shop regularly can save some money, and I do not think people should stop using these programs. However, the fact that nearly every large company offers one suggests that the programs earn them far more than they give away. Otherwise, businesses would not continue investing so much in them.
questions.tk: Your professor is teaching a class on economics. Write a post responding to the professor's question. In your response, you should do the following: express and support your opinion, and make a contribution to the discussion in your own words. An effective response will contain at least 100 words.
pt: Takes Ethan's position and refers to him by name
Adds a new reason: companies gain valuable data about customer habits
Acknowledges Rosa's experience by name and keeps a fair tone

ps.name: Rosa
ps.text: Loyalty programs mainly benefit consumers. My family shops at the same supermarket every week anyway, so the points we collect are basically free money. Last year we saved enough to get a large discount on a new kettle. If you are going to buy something regularly, it makes sense to be rewarded for it.

ps.name: Ethan
ps.text: Companies are the real winners. The rewards are usually small, but they persuade people to keep shopping at one store even when another store has lower prices. Customers end up paying more overall, and they often buy extra products just to reach the next reward level.

questions.s: Last month you booked a table for eight people at an Italian restaurant called Casa Lena to celebrate your sister's birthday. You received a confirmation email at the time. However, when your group arrived on Saturday evening, the staff said they had no record of your booking, and you waited almost an hour for a table. You want to write to the restaurant's manager, Mr. Romano.
questions.e:
Dear Mr. Romano,
I am writing about my visit to Casa Lena last Saturday evening. I had booked a table for eight people at 7 p.m. to celebrate my sister's birthday, and I received a confirmation email when I made the reservation. However, when we arrived, the staff told us there was no record of our booking.
We ended up waiting almost an hour before a table was free. My sister's birthday dinner started very late, two older relatives became quite tired, and the evening was much more stressful than we had hoped.
I have attached the confirmation email so that you can check what went wrong. I would appreciate an explanation, and I would also like to ask whether the restaurant could offer a partial refund or a discount on a future visit.
Thank you for taking the time to read this.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe what happened when you arrived.
Explain how this affected your celebration.
Ask the restaurant to do something about it.
questions.tk: Write an email to the restaurant manager. In your email, do the following:
pt: Gives clear facts about the booking and what happened on arrival.
Explains the effect on the celebration in a calm, specific way.
Supports the complaint with evidence (the confirmation email).
Makes a reasonable request and keeps a polite, formal tone.

questions.s: You are taking a sociology course, and quizzes are graded by the teaching assistant, Olga. Yesterday you got your third quiz back with a score of 14 out of 20. When you added up the points written next to each question, however, the total came to 17. You also think one of your short answers may have been marked wrong by mistake, because it matches the definition in the textbook.
questions.e:
Dear Olga,
I hope you are having a good week. I am writing about my score on Quiz 3, which I received back in class yesterday. The score at the top of the page is 14 out of 20, but when I added up the points next to each question, the total came to 17. I think there may have been a small error in the addition.
I also have a question about question 6. My answer was marked incorrect, but it seems to match the definition of "social mobility" on page 84 of the textbook.
Would you be willing to look at the quiz again? I could bring it to your office hours on Wednesday, or I could leave a copy in your mailbox in the department office, whichever is easier for you.
Thank you very much for your time.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain what you noticed about your quiz score.
Describe the second problem you found.
Ask her to review the quiz and suggest how.
questions.tk: Write an email to the teaching assistant. In your email, do the following:
pt: Explains the scoring error with exact numbers.
Raises the second issue politely and supports it with evidence from the textbook.
Asks for a review and offers convenient ways to share the quiz.
Uses a respectful tone that does not accuse the teaching assistant.

questions.s: You are the events coordinator for your university's international student club. The club wants to hold a picnic in Greenfield Park next month to welcome new members, and you expect about forty people. The city's Parks Department website says that groups of more than twenty-five must reserve a picnic area, but it does not explain the rules about food, music or cost. You decide to email the Parks Department.
questions.e:
Dear Parks Department,
I am the events coordinator for the International Student Club at the university. We are planning a welcome picnic for new members in Greenfield Park next month, and we expect about forty people to attend. Your website says that groups of more than twenty-five must reserve a picnic area, so I am writing to ask about the process.
Could you please tell me what rules apply to large groups? In particular, I would like to know whether we may bring our own food and a small portable grill, whether quiet music is allowed, and how much the reservation costs.
Our first choice would be Saturday the 14th, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. If that date is not available, Sunday the 15th or Saturday the 21st at the same time would also work for us.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe the event you are planning.
Ask about the rules for groups.
Give details of the dates you would prefer.
questions.tk: Write an email to the city's Parks Department. In your email, do the following:
pt: Introduces the writer's role and describes the event with useful numbers.
Asks clear, specific questions about the rules.
Gives a first choice and alternative dates with times.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a city office.

questions.s: You are doing an internship in the research department of a software company. Your supervisor, Mr. Osei, asked you to collect and organize customer feedback for a new mobile app, and he expected the task to take three weeks. You finished it in two weeks. You enjoyed the work, and you have noticed that the design team is preparing user tests that you would like to learn about.
questions.e:
Dear Mr. Osei,
I wanted to let you know that I have finished organizing the customer feedback for the new mobile app. I sorted more than three hundred comments into categories, such as speed, design and payment problems, and I added a one-page summary of the most common issues. The file is in our shared team folder.
Since I finished a week earlier than planned, I would be glad to take on a new task. I have really enjoyed working with the customer data, and I would like to keep learning as much as possible during my internship.
If it is possible, I would be very interested in helping the design team with their upcoming user tests. I could help to recruit participants, take notes during the sessions, or compare the results with the feedback I have already collected.
Thank you for your guidance.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Tell him what you have finished.
Ask for a new task.
Suggest a project you would like to help with.
questions.tk: Write an email to your internship supervisor. In your email, do the following:
pt: Reports the completed work with specific, impressive details.
Asks for more work in a positive, professional way.
Suggests a relevant project and explains how the writer could contribute.
Uses a polite, confident tone suitable for a supervisor.

questions.s: Your university library lets students reserve group study rooms through an online booking system. Last Tuesday you reserved a room for your project group from 2 to 4 p.m. and received a confirmation. When your group arrived, another group was already using the room, and they also had a confirmation for the same time. The front desk could not find another free room, so your group had to work in a noisy café.
questions.e:
Dear Library Staff,
I am writing about a problem with the study room booking system. Last Tuesday I reserved Room 2C from 2 to 4 p.m. for my project group and received a confirmation email. When we arrived, however, another group was already in the room, and they had a confirmation for exactly the same time.
The front desk staff were very helpful, but there were no other rooms available, so we had to work in a crowded café nearby. Because it was so noisy, we could not practice our presentation, which we have to give in class this Friday.
It seems that the system allowed two bookings for the same room. Would it be possible to add a check that stops this from happening? It might also help if the confirmation email included a code that students could show at the desk.
Thank you for looking into this.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe what happened last Tuesday.
Explain why this was a problem for your group.
Suggest a change to the booking system.
questions.tk: Write an email to the library's front desk staff. In your email, do the following:
pt: Describes the double booking clearly with the room and time.
Explains the consequence for the group's work.
Offers a constructive, specific suggestion for the system.
Stays polite and even thanks the staff, rather than blaming them.

questions.s: You rent a house with two roommates. Last week the kitchen faucet started leaking, and now water drips constantly, even when the handle is turned off. This morning you noticed a dark stain on the cabinet under the sink, and the wood feels soft. Your landlord, Mrs. Thompson, lives in another town and usually prefers that tenants contact her by email. You are worried that the damage will get worse.
questions.e:
Dear Mrs. Thompson,
I am writing to let you know about a problem in the kitchen at 18 Willow Lane. Last week the kitchen faucet started leaking, and now it drips all the time, even when it is turned off completely. This morning I also found a dark stain on the cabinet under the sink, and the wood there feels soft.
To stop more damage, I have placed a bowl under the pipe and moved everything out of the cabinet so that it can dry. I also took photos of the faucet and the cabinet, which I have attached to this email.
Could you please arrange for a plumber to come as soon as possible? My roommates and I are usually at home in the mornings before 10 a.m., and someone will be there all day on Thursday.
Thank you very much.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe the problem in the kitchen.
Explain what you have done so far.
Ask her to arrange a repair and say when you are home.

Shows responsible action already taken (the bowl, the photos).
Makes a clear request with specific availability for the repair.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a landlord.

questions.s: Next month you will attend a three-day conference on renewable energy for students and young researchers. You registered online two weeks ago and paid the student fee of ninety dollars. Yesterday you checked your bank statement and saw that the fee had been charged twice. You also realized that you forgot to choose a workshop during registration. The conference has a contact email for its registration team.
questions.e:

I registered online for the Renewable Energy Student Conference two weeks ago and paid the student fee of ninety dollars. Yesterday, however, I checked my bank statement and noticed that the fee was charged twice on the same day, so I have paid one hundred eighty dollars in total.
Could you please check my registration and refund the extra payment? My registration number is RE-2241, and I would be happy to send a copy of my bank statement if that would help.

questions.s: Last weekend your friend Aisha lent you her bicycle so that you could ride to a job interview across town. On the way back, you rode over broken glass, and the front tire got a flat. You walked the bike home, and it is now in your building's storage room. Aisha needs the bike to get to her classes starting next Monday, and you want to make things right.
questions.e:
Hi Aisha,
Thanks again for lending me your bike on Saturday. The interview went really well! Unfortunately, on the way home I rode over some broken glass, and the front tire got a flat. I had to walk the rest of the way, so the bike is in my building's storage room right now.
I'm really sorry about this. I know you need the bike for classes next week, so I'm going to take it to the repair shop on Hill Street tomorrow and get a new tire and tube. Of course, I'll pay for everything.
The shop says it should be ready by Friday afternoon. Could I bring it over to your place on Friday at around 6 p.m.? If that doesn't work, I could drop it off on Saturday morning instead.
Thanks for understanding!
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Tell her what happened to the bicycle.
Apologize and explain how you will fix the problem.
Suggest a time to return the bicycle.

Suggests specific times to return the bike, with an alternative.

questions.s: You joined your university's language exchange program, which matches students so they can practice each other's languages. You were matched with a partner named Chen, and the program asked you to meet once a week for one hour. Over the past month, Chen has canceled three of your four meetings at the last minute. You still want to practice Mandarin. The program is run by a coordinator, Ms. Patel.
questions.e:
Dear Ms. Patel,
I am writing about my experience in the language exchange program this semester. I was matched with a partner named Chen, and we agreed to meet every Thursday afternoon. However, over the past month, three of our four meetings were canceled at the last minute.
I am sure Chen is very busy, and I do not want to cause any problems for him. Still, I joined the program because I want to improve my spoken Mandarin before a study abroad semester next year, and regular conversation practice is the most useful thing for me.
Would it be possible to be matched with a second partner, or with a different partner whose schedule fits better? I am free on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons and on Saturday mornings. Alternatively, a small group session could also work well.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe the problem with your language exchange.
Explain what you hope to get from the program.
Suggest a solution.
questions.tk: Write an email to the program coordinator. In your email, do the following:
pt: Describes the problem factually without criticizing the partner unfairly.
Explains the writer's goals, which makes the request reasonable.
Suggests specific solutions and gives availability.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a program coordinator.

questions.s: You work part-time at a bookstore in the city center, and your shift on Saturday was supposed to start at 9 a.m. On the way to work, the bus you were on broke down, and you had to wait forty minutes for another one. Your phone battery was also dead, so you could not call the store. You arrived an hour late. Your manager, Ms. Hughes, was not at the store that day.
questions.e:
Dear Ms. Hughes,
I am writing to explain why I arrived an hour late for my shift last Saturday. On the way to work, the bus I was on broke down, and I had to wait forty minutes for the next one. Unfortunately, my phone battery had also run out, so I could not call the store to let anyone know.
I am very sorry for the trouble this caused. As soon as I arrived, I apologized to Lucas, who had been working alone, and I stayed an extra hour after my shift to help unpack the new delivery.
In the future, I will take an earlier bus on weekend mornings so that I have more time if there is a delay. I will also carry a portable phone charger so that I can always contact the store.
Thank you for your understanding.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain why you arrived late.
Apologize and describe what you did when you arrived.
Explain how you will avoid this problem in the future.
questions.tk: Write an email to your manager, Ms. Hughes. In your email, do the following:
pt: Explains the cause of the delay clearly and honestly.
Apologizes and shows responsibility through actions taken that day.
Describes specific steps to prevent the problem in the future.
Uses a respectful, professional tone suitable for an employer.

questions.s: You are taking a history course with Professor Okafor. For the final project, the professor put you in a group of four students who must give a presentation together in two weeks. Last week your group held two planning meetings, but one member, Lucas, did not come to either of them and has not answered any messages. Without his part of the research, the group cannot finish the slides on time. You want to ask the professor for advice.
questions.e:
Dear Professor Okafor,
I am writing about my group's final project for your history course. One of our four members, Lucas, has not been able to take part so far, and we are worried about finishing the presentation on time.
Last week we held two planning meetings, and Lucas did not attend either one. We have also sent him several messages and emails, but he has not replied. Because his section covers the economic background, the rest of the slides depend on it.
Could you advise us on how to handle this? One possible solution would be for the three of us to divide his section and present it ourselves, with each person's contribution noted on the final slide. If you prefer a different approach, we would be happy to follow it.
Thank you for your time.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain the problem your group is having.
Describe what the group has already tried.
Ask the professor for advice or suggest a possible solution.
questions.tk: Write an email to Professor Okafor. In your email, do the following:
pt: States the problem clearly in the first paragraph without blaming Lucas in a rude way.
Gives concrete details of what the group has tried (two meetings, several messages).
Makes a specific, reasonable suggestion and still leaves the decision to the professor.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a professor, with a clear greeting and closing.

questions.s: You rent a small apartment near the university. Three days ago the heating system in your apartment stopped working, and the nights have become very cold. You called the landlord, Ms. Rivera, twice, but both times you reached her voicemail and she has not called back. You have an important exam next week and need to study at home in the evenings. You decide to send her an email instead.
questions.e:
Dear Ms. Rivera,
I am writing because the heating in my apartment, unit 4B, stopped working three days ago. I tried to call you twice, but I reached your voicemail, so I thought an email might be easier.
The radiators are completely cold, even when the thermostat is set to the highest temperature. At night the apartment becomes very cold, and it is difficult to sleep. I also have an important exam next week, and I need to study at home in the evenings, which is hard in these conditions.
I would be grateful if a repair person could come as soon as possible. I am at home every day after 3 p.m., and I am free all day on Saturday. If another time is better, please let me know and I will try to arrange it.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe the problem with the heating.
Explain how the problem is affecting you.
Give details of when you are available for a repair visit.
questions.tk: Write an email to your landlord, Ms. Rivera. In your email, do the following:
pt: Identifies the apartment and the problem precisely (what stopped working and when).
Explains the effect on daily life and studying without sounding angry.
Gives clear, specific times when a repair visit is possible.
Stays polite and formal while making the urgency clear.

questions.s: You work part-time at a café on campus. Your manager, Mr. Chen, makes the staff schedule two weeks in advance. Yesterday the university published the final exam timetable, and you found out that two of your exams are on mornings when you are scheduled to work. One of them is on a Tuesday and the other on the following Thursday. You do not want to leave your coworkers short of staff.

I hope you are well. Yesterday the university released the final exam timetable, and I have found that two of my exams fall on mornings when I am scheduled to work: Tuesday the 9th and Thursday the 11th.
I am sorry for the short notice. Would it be possible to move me off those two morning shifts? I understand that exam weeks are busy at the café, so I do not want to leave the team short.
I would be happy to work extra afternoon or evening shifts that week to make up the hours. I have also spoken with Amara, who said she could take the Tuesday morning if you agree. I can check with other coworkers about Thursday as well.
Thank you for considering my request.
Best regards,
Sam

Ask for a change to your schedule.
Suggest a way to cover your shifts.
questions.tk: Write an email to your manager, Mr. Chen. In your email, do the following:

Asks for the change politely and acknowledges the inconvenience.
Offers a practical solution, such as swapping shifts or working extra hours.
Keeps a respectful, professional tone suitable for an employer.

questions.s: Last week you ordered a desk lamp from an online home goods store called Brightway. The lamp arrived yesterday, but the glass shade was cracked and the switch did not work when you plugged it in. You still need a lamp for your desk because you often study late at night. The store's website says customers can contact the customer service team by email about damaged items.

questions.s: You are a member of the campus photography club. The club meets every Wednesday evening, and members borrow cameras and lighting equipment from a storage room in the art building. The professor does not post lecture notes online. Your classmate Priya sits next to you in class and always takes very detailed notes. questions.e:

In return, I'd be happy to help with the lab report due Friday. I've already finished the data analysis section, so we could go through the graphs together at the library if that would be useful.
Thanks so much!
Best regards,
Sam

Offer something in return.
questions.tk: Write an email to your classmate Priya. In your email, do the following:

Offers a fair, concrete favor in return.

questions.s: You live on Maple Street, a quiet residential road near a public park. For about two weeks, two of the streetlights on your block have not been working, so the sidewalk is very dark in the evening. Many people, including children and older residents, walk to the park after sunset. The city's Public Works Office has an email address for reporting problems with streets and lighting.
questions.e:
Dear Public Works Office,
I am writing to report two broken streetlights on Maple Street. They are on the block between Elm Avenue and the entrance to Riverside Park, one in front of number 42 and the other near the bus stop. Neither light has worked for about two weeks.
This section of the street is now very dark after sunset. Many residents, including children and older people, walk to the park in the evening, and it is difficult to see the uneven parts of the sidewalk. I am concerned that someone could fall or feel unsafe.
Could you please let me know whether a repair has been scheduled and approximately when the work will be done? If you need more information, I would be glad to help.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.
Best regards,
Sam

Explain why the problem is important to fix.
Ask what the office will do and when.
questions.tk: Write an email to the city's Public Works Office. In your email, do the following:
pt: Gives the exact location so the office can find the problem easily.
Explains the safety concern with specific details about who is affected.

Uses a polite, formal tone appropriate for a government office.

questions.s: Two weeks ago you borrowed three books from the university library. You returned all of them on time by putting them in the book drop outside the main entrance. However, yesterday you received an email saying that one of the books, a guide to statistics, is overdue and that you owe a fine of eight dollars. You are sure you returned it with the others on the same evening.
questions.e:
Dear Circulation Desk Staff,
I am writing about a fine on my library account. Two weeks ago I borrowed three books, and I returned all of them on the evening of October 12 by putting them in the book drop outside the main entrance. This was two days before the due date.
Yesterday, however, I received an email saying that one of the books, Practical Statistics for Beginners, is overdue and that I owe eight dollars. The other two books were checked in correctly, so I believe this one may have been missed or placed on the wrong shelf.
Could you please check the shelves and the return area for this book? If you find it, I would appreciate it if you could remove the fine from my account. My student ID number is 2047731.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain what you did with the books.
Describe the problem with your account.
Ask the library to take a specific action.
questions.tk: Write an email to the library's circulation desk. In your email, do the following:
pt: Gives a clear account of when and how the books were returned.
Describes the problem with specific details (which book, the amount of the fine).
Suggests a possible explanation politely instead of accusing the staff.
Asks for a concrete action and provides information needed to find the account.

questions.s: You are a graduate student, and your poster about water quality in local rivers was accepted for a regional environmental science conference. The organizers scheduled your poster session for Friday at 9 a.m. Yesterday the airline changed your flight, and you will now arrive on Friday at around noon. The conference continues until Saturday afternoon. You want to contact the conference organizers, led by Dr. Mendes.
questions.e:
Dear Dr. Mendes,
Thank you again for accepting my poster, "Seasonal Changes in Water Quality in Local Rivers," for this year's conference. Unfortunately, I am writing because of an unexpected travel problem.
Yesterday my airline changed my flight, and I will now arrive in the city at around noon on Friday. As a result, I will not be able to present at my scheduled poster session at 9 a.m. that day.
Would it be possible to move my poster to a later session? I will be available any time from 2 p.m. on Friday until the end of the conference on Saturday afternoon. If no other session has space, I could also hang my poster on Friday afternoon and stand by it during a break.
I apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your help.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain your situation.
Ask for a change to your poster session.
Give details of when you will be available.
questions.tk: Write an email to the conference organizers. In your email, do the following:
pt: Explains the travel change clearly and early in the email.
Makes a polite, specific request for a different session.
Gives exact availability so the organizers can easily find a new slot.
Offers a flexible alternative and keeps a formal, professional tone.

questions.s: You are doing a summer internship at a marketing company. Your supervisor is Ms. Adeyemi. Your university has just announced that the graduation ceremony will take place on a Thursday next month, and your family is traveling from another city to attend. You will need to take that Thursday and the following Friday off. You are currently helping your team prepare a report that is due at the end of that month.
questions.e:
Dear Ms. Adeyemi,
I hope you are having a good week. I am writing to ask about taking two days off next month. My university has just announced that the graduation ceremony will be held on Thursday the 18th, and my family is traveling from another city to attend.
Would it be possible for me to take Thursday the 18th and Friday the 19th off? I wanted to ask well in advance so that the team can plan around my absence.
I know the client report is due at the end of the month. To make sure it stays on schedule, I plan to finish my section on social media data by Tuesday the 16th. I could also stay a little later on the days before I leave if that would help.
Thank you for considering my request.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain why you need time off.
Ask for permission to take the days off.
Explain how you will make sure your work is done.
questions.tk: Write an email to your internship supervisor. In your email, do the following:
pt: Gives the reason and the exact dates clearly.
Asks for permission politely rather than simply announcing the absence.
Shows responsibility with a specific plan for finishing the work.
Uses a professional, respectful tone appropriate for a workplace supervisor.

questions.s: You are taking a chemistry course with Professor Lindqvist, and a research paper based on your own lab experiment is due next Monday. Last week the machine you needed to measure your samples broke down, and the lab technician says it will not be repaired until Wednesday. Without these measurements, you cannot complete the results section of your paper. You have already finished the introduction and the methods section.
questions.e:
Dear Professor Lindqvist,
I am writing about the research paper that is due next Monday. Last week the spectrometer that I need to measure my samples broke down. The lab technician told me it will not be repaired until Wednesday, so I have not been able to collect the data for my results section.
I have already finished the introduction and the methods section, and my samples are prepared and stored correctly. As soon as the machine is working again, I can complete the measurements in one afternoon.
Would it be possible to have a short extension? I would suggest Friday of next week as a new deadline, which would give me enough time to analyze the data and write the discussion carefully. I am also happy to send you my finished sections now.
Thank you for your understanding.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain what happened in the lab.
Describe the progress you have made so far.
Ask for an extension and suggest a new deadline.
questions.tk: Write an email to Professor Lindqvist. In your email, do the following:
pt: Explains the cause of the delay clearly and shows it was outside the student's control.
Shows progress with specific details, which makes the request more convincing.
Requests a specific, reasonable new deadline instead of an open-ended extension.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a professor.

questions.s: You rent an apartment from Mr. Kowalski, and your one-year lease ends in August. This summer you have been offered a three-month research position in another city, from June to August. You would like to keep your apartment for next year, but you do not want to pay rent for an empty apartment while you are away. A friend of yours, Mateo, is looking for a place to stay for the summer.
questions.e:
Dear Mr. Kowalski,
I hope you are doing well. I am writing to ask about my apartment for this summer. I have been offered a research position in another city from June 1 to August 31, and I plan to accept it. However, I would very much like to renew my lease and stay in the apartment next year.
Would you allow me to sublet the apartment while I am away? I would continue to be responsible for the rent and for any damage, and I would make sure everything is in good condition when I return.
The person who would stay there is my friend Mateo, a graduate student in engineering. He is quiet and tidy, does not smoke, and has no pets. He would be happy to meet you before June if you would like.
Thank you for considering this.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain your plans for the summer.
Ask whether you are allowed to sublet the apartment.
Give details about the person who would stay there.
questions.tk: Write an email to your landlord, Mr. Kowalski. In your email, do the following:
pt: Explains the summer plans and the dates clearly.
Asks permission directly and politely, and shows the tenant will stay responsible.
Gives reassuring, relevant details about the subtenant.
Uses a respectful, formal tone appropriate for a landlord.

questions.s: You are a member of the campus recreation center and have signed up for an evening yoga class that meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays. In the past three weeks, the class has been canceled four times, and each time the notice was posted on the website less than an hour before it was supposed to start. You paid a fee for the whole semester. You want to contact the center's program manager, Ms. Haddad.
questions.e:
Dear Ms. Haddad,
I am writing about the evening yoga class on Tuesdays and Thursdays, which I signed up for this semester. Over the past three weeks, the class has been canceled four times. Each time, the notice appeared on the website less than an hour before the start.
These late cancellations have been frustrating. Twice I had already walked to the center from the library when I found out, and I had planned my study schedule around the class. Since I paid for the whole semester, I feel I am missing much of what I paid for.
I would like to suggest two changes. First, could the center send a text or email to students as soon as a class is canceled? Second, it would be helpful to have a substitute instructor or a make-up session when the regular teacher cannot come.
Thank you for your attention.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe what has happened with the class.
Explain how this has affected you.
Suggest a way to improve the situation.
questions.tk: Write an email to the program manager. In your email, do the following:
pt: Summarizes the problem with clear numbers and timing.
Explains the personal effect without exaggerating or sounding rude.
Offers constructive, specific suggestions rather than only complaining.
Keeps a polite, formal tone suitable for a program manager.

questions.s: You and your friend Kwame planned a weekend trip to a lake about two hours away. You were going to drive there on Saturday morning in your car and come back on Sunday evening. Yesterday a mechanic told you that your car needs a repair that will take several days. You still want to go on the trip, and you know there is a bus that goes near the lake.
questions.e:
Hi Kwame,
I've got some bad news about our lake trip. I took my car to the garage yesterday because the brakes were making a strange noise, and the mechanic said it needs a repair that will take at least four days. So the car definitely won't be ready by Saturday.
That means we can't drive there the way we planned, and we'd also need to rethink how to carry the tent and the cooler.
I still really want to go, though! I checked online, and there's a bus that leaves the central station at 8:30 on Saturday morning and stops about a mile from the lake. Tickets are only twelve dollars each. We'd just need to pack lighter. What do you think? If you'd rather wait, we could also go the following weekend.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Tell him what happened to your car.
Explain how this affects your plans.
Suggest a different way to make the trip.
questions.tk: Write an email to your friend Kwame. In your email, do the following:
pt: Explains the car problem briefly and clearly.
Shows how the change affects the original plan.
Suggests a practical alternative with useful details (time, price).
Uses a relaxed, friendly tone with contractions, suitable for a friend.

questions.s: For your economics course, you ordered a textbook from the campus bookstore's website. The course list says students need the fifth edition, but the book you received last week is the fourth edition. The professor has already assigned homework from chapter twelve, which does not exist in the older edition. The first homework set is due in five days, and you have not been able to start it.
questions.e:
Dear Customer Service Team,
I am writing about my online order number 71904. I ordered the fifth edition of Principles of Economics for my course, as listed on the required reading page. However, the book I received last week is the fourth edition.
This has caused a problem with my coursework. My professor has assigned homework from chapter twelve, which does not exist in the older edition. The first assignment is due in five days, and I have not been able to start it.
Could you please exchange the book for the correct edition as soon as possible? I can bring the fourth edition to the store tomorrow, so it would be ideal if I could pick up the fifth edition at the same time. If it is out of stock, please let me know when it will arrive.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain what you ordered and what you received.
Describe the problem this has caused.
Ask for a specific solution.
questions.tk: Write an email to the bookstore's customer service department. In your email, do the following:
pt: Clearly contrasts what was ordered with what was received.
Explains why the mistake matters, with the deadline as a detail.
Asks for a clear exchange and suggests how it could happen quickly.
Uses a polite, businesslike tone.

questions.s: You volunteer at the city's natural history museum, where you guide school groups on Saturdays. The volunteer coordinator, Mr. Abara, has announced a required training session next Saturday morning about the museum's new dinosaur exhibit. However, you will be taking a university entrance exam that morning, which you registered for months ago. You want to stay in the volunteer program and lead tours of the new exhibit.
questions.e:
Dear Mr. Abara,
Thank you for organizing the training session on the new dinosaur exhibit next Saturday. Unfortunately, I will not be able to attend, because I am taking a university entrance exam that morning. I registered for the exam several months ago, and it cannot be moved.
I am very sorry to miss it, because I really enjoy guiding school groups and I am excited about the new exhibit. I would love to lead tours of it once it opens.
Would it be possible for me to catch up in another way? For example, I could join a later session if there is one, or I could come in on a weekday afternoon and follow an experienced guide through the exhibit. If there are any training materials or slides, I would also be happy to study them at home.
Thank you for understanding.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain why you cannot attend the training.
Show that you still want to take part in the program.
Suggest another way for you to receive the training.
questions.tk: Write an email to the volunteer coordinator. In your email, do the following:
pt: Gives a clear, acceptable reason for missing the required session.
Shows enthusiasm and commitment to the volunteer role.
Suggests one or more realistic alternatives for catching up.
Uses a polite, appreciative tone suitable for a coordinator.

questions.s: You live in a university residence hall. For the past ten days, the wireless internet on your floor has been extremely slow in the evenings and often disconnects completely. Many students on your floor have the same problem. You take two online courses this semester, and last night you were disconnected in the middle of an online quiz. You decide to write to the Student Housing Office.
questions.e:
Dear Student Housing Office,
I live on the third floor of Hillside Hall, room 312, and I am writing about the wireless internet on our floor. For about ten days, the connection has been very slow in the evenings, especially between 7 and 11 p.m., and it often disconnects completely. Several other students on my floor have noticed the same problem.
This is seriously affecting my studies. I am taking two online courses this semester, and most of the lectures and quizzes take place in the evening. Last night I was disconnected in the middle of an online quiz and lost several answers.
Could you please ask the technical team to check the network equipment on our floor? In the meantime, it would help to know whether there is a study area in the building with a more reliable connection.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe the problem with the internet.
Explain how it is affecting your studies.
Ask the office to take action.
questions.tk: Write an email to the Student Housing Office. In your email, do the following:
pt: Gives precise information about the location and the timing of the problem.
Mentions that other students are affected, which shows it is not an isolated issue.
Explains the academic impact with a concrete example.
Makes a clear, polite request and asks about a temporary solution.

questions.s: You are a second-year student studying psychology. To graduate on time, you must take a research methods course this coming semester. When you tried to register online this morning, the system said the course was full, and the waiting list already has fifteen names. Your academic advisor, Dr. Nakamura, helps students plan their courses and can sometimes give special permission to join a class.
questions.e:
Dear Dr. Nakamura,
I hope you are well. I am writing because I tried to register this morning for Research Methods in Psychology, but the system showed that the course is full. The waiting list already has fifteen students on it.
This course is very important for me, because it is required for my major and it is a prerequisite for two courses I plan to take next year. If I cannot take it this semester, I am worried that I will not be able to graduate on time.
Could you help me find a solution? One option might be special permission to join one of the existing sections. Alternatively, if a new section is opened, I would be happy to take it at any time, including early mornings or evenings. I could also meet you during your office hours to discuss my plan.
Thank you very much.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain the problem with registration.
Explain why the course is important for you.
Ask for help and suggest possible options.
questions.tk: Write an email to your academic advisor, Dr. Nakamura. In your email, do the following:
pt: Describes the registration problem with clear facts.
Explains the importance of the course for graduation and future courses.
Asks politely for help and suggests realistic options.
Uses a formal tone appropriate for a faculty advisor.

questions.s: You are a member of the university debate club, which meets every Monday at 4 p.m. This semester, many members are taking science courses with labs that run until 5 p.m. on Mondays, so attendance at meetings has dropped from about twenty students to eight. The club has an important regional competition in two months. You want to write to the club leader, Sofia, about the meeting time.
questions.e:
Hi Sofia,
I wanted to share something I've noticed about our Monday meetings. This semester, attendance has dropped from around twenty people to only eight. After talking to a few members, I found out that many of them have science labs on Mondays that don't finish until 5 p.m., so they simply can't make it.
This is worrying because the regional competition is only two months away. If half the team misses our practice debates, it'll be hard to prepare everyone properly and choose strong teams.
Would you consider moving our meetings? Wednesday at 6 p.m. might work, since the classrooms in the humanities building are free then. To make sure it suits most people, we could send a quick online poll with two or three possible times and pick the most popular one.
Let me know what you think!
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Describe the problem with attendance.
Explain why it matters now.
Suggest a new meeting time and a way to choose it.
questions.tk: Write an email to the club leader. In your email, do the following:
pt: Describes the drop in attendance with numbers and a reason.
Connects the problem to the upcoming competition.
Suggests a specific new time and a fair way to decide.
Uses a friendly, cooperative tone suitable for a student leader.

questions.s: You are in a study group with three classmates for your statistics course. The group meets every Thursday evening, and this week it is your turn to host the meeting in your apartment. However, the building's management has just told residents that water will be shut off on Thursday evening for pipe repairs. You want the group to meet anyway, because there is a test on Monday. You email your classmate Yuki, who organizes the group.
questions.e:
Hi Yuki,
I'm afraid I can't host our study group this Thursday after all. My building just announced that the water will be shut off on Thursday evening for pipe repairs, so there won't be any water in my apartment for coffee or even the bathroom!
I still think we should meet, though, especially with the statistics test on Monday. How about booking one of the group study rooms on the second floor of the library? They're free to reserve online, and they have big whiteboards, which would be perfect for working through problems together.
To make up for not hosting, I'll bring snacks for everyone. I can also print copies of last year's practice test and prepare a short summary sheet of the formulas from chapters six and seven.
Let me know if that works for everyone.
Best regards,
Sam
bl: Explain why you cannot host the meeting.
Suggest another place to meet.
Give details of what you can bring or prepare.
questions.tk: Write an email to your classmate Yuki. In your email, do the following:
pt: Explains the reason for the change briefly and clearly.
Suggests a convenient alternative location with a reason it works well.
Offers specific, useful contributions to the meeting.
Uses a friendly, informal tone with contractions, suitable for a classmate.
